question.text: Which bond provides the PERFECT immunization against interest rate risk for a 10-year liability, theoretically?

explanation.text: The Logic: A zero-coupon bond has Duration = Maturity (no intermediate cash flows to reinvest). It eliminates BOTH price risk (held to maturity) AND reinvestment risk (no coupons). Theoretically perfect immunization for a matched liability. The Trap: 10-year coupon bond has duration < 10 years (typical ~7). 20-year bond with duration 10 has reinvestment risk on coupons. Cross-Exam Context: Same concept in IV; XXI-B expects strong reasoning. Manager's Pro-Tip: In India, zero-coupon Gsecs are rare beyond Strips/zero-coupon PSU bonds — PMs typically approximate with duration-matched portfolios.
